grandparents_cupboard.reason: Oats, milk, eggs, butter, honey, natural yoghurt, fruit and spices are all plain kitchen staples with nothing factory-made.

supermarket.reason: Forced rhubarb is stocked by mainstream supermarkets in January at an everyday price, and everything else is basic.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a baking dish, bowl, grater and whisk, with simple mixing and baking.

works.reason: 200g oats to about 450ml liquid with two eggs, baked at 190°C for 35 minutes, gives a properly set baked oats for four, sweetened enough by honey and clementine against the rhubarb.

honest_times.reason: Fifteen minutes covers zesting, juicing, whisking, cutting the rhubarb and peeling and slicing three clementines, and the 35 minute bake matches the steps.

honest_ingredients.reason: Forced rhubarb is the same food as the rhubarb id, and every listed ingredient and seasoning is used with nothing extra brought in.

seasonal_feel.reason: A warm baked breakfast suits mid-January, and the clementines flavour the custard and cover the top rather than serving as a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are clear, plain British English a beginner could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: Oats, eggs, milk, fruit and yoghurt make a filling, wholesome breakfast with only modest added honey.
